target_customer: Small software teams that skip writing end to end tests
problem: Developers delay tests to ship features and then hit production bugs; Autotest generated integration tests for a website with little effort.
product_category: Automated end to end website testing

founders.name: Ben Share
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page; now at Coast.

founders.name: Aaron Barbieri-Aghib
education: University of Chicago, math and biology

exit.reason: Not stated; YC lists Inactive and dime.io redirects to a domain for sale page.

competitors.name: ProdPerfect
competitors.what: Autonomous end to end web testing built from live user traffic

competitors.name: Reflect
competitors.what: Cloud no code end to end web testing
competitors.funding_then: $1.8M seed, Jan 2021, Battery and Craft led

competitors.name: mabl
competitors.funding_then: $40M Series C announced Nov 2021, $77M total (after the batch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating reliable tests automatically from a site needs recorders and flake handling; hard to make robust but within reach of two engineers.

defensibility.rationale: Funded rivals already offered similar no code testing and the product had no data or integration lock in described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded testing vendors kept growing (mabl raised $40M in Nov 2021) while Dime went inactive.

market_need_then: The YC description states developers skip tests under shipping pressure; competitor raises in 2019 to 2021 show spend on automated testing.

branding.domain_note: dime.io, a .io domain; now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is shared by several unrelated companies, including another YC Dime; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Dime built Autotest, an automatic end to end testing tool, in YC Summer 2021 with two founders. Reflect, ProdPerfect and mabl were already funded in the same niche, and Dime shows only a small seed round in databases. YC lists it inactive and the domain is for sale, but no founder post-mortem was found, so the factors are inferred.
notes: CB Insights pages conflict ($130K seed with YC and Soma Capital; another page says $500K over 3 rounds with a Tekedia investor in 2024, possibly a different Dime). The $130K figure rests on a single database and is unverified; no date given. dime.io redirects to a domain sale page. mabl source is dated about 3 months after the batch. Outcome cause not public.
